Architecture

localgpu: two independent process trees, plus a one-shot CLI, sharing one Ollama. Verified against source on 2026-09-06; see comments for path:line. Tree A redrawn at ac93221d: setup step 6 no longer hand-substitutes

flowchart TB

    subgraph TreeA["Tree A - MCP path (per repo, agent-driven setup)"]
        direction TB
        CC1["Claude Code<br/>(main session)"]
        Setup["/localgpu:setup step 6<br/>plugin/localgpu/commands/setup.md:114<br/>*one command - no template, no<br/>placeholder substitution by the agent*"]
        McpInit["localgpu mcp-init &lt;repo&gt;<br/>cmd_mcp_init() resolves<br/>all three paths literally"]
        MCPJson[".mcp.json<br/>*written to repo root by mcp-init -<br/>gitignored by default (:426),<br/>not checked into THIS repo*"]
        Server["mcp/server.py<br/>plugin/localgpu/mcp/server.py:1 - stdio MCP server,<br/>3 tools: search_code, index_status,<br/>index_refresh"]

        CC1 -- "spawns stdio child via<br/>install venv's python<br/>(command from .mcp.json)" --> Server
        Setup -- "runs the console script from<br/>the install venv - a script now, not the agent" --> McpInit
        McpInit -- "serialises the whole doc, THEN opens<br/>plugin/localgpu/cli/localgpu_cli.py:421-422" --> MCPJson
        MCPJson -. "read by Claude Code<br/>to know how to spawn Server" .-> CC1
    end

    subgraph TreeB["Tree B - localgpu shell path (interactive, CLI-driven)"]
        direction TB
        User(["user runs<br/>`localgpu shell`"])
        CLI["cli/localgpu_cli.py:112<br/>cmd_shell()"]
        ProxyThread["anthropic_proxy server<br/>plugin/localgpu/cli/localgpu_cli.py:119-131<br/>threading.Thread(daemon=True)<br/>*background thread, NOT a subprocess*"]
        CC2["second Claude Code session<br/>plugin/localgpu/cli/localgpu_cli.py:141<br/>subprocess.run([claude, ...])<br/>ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL -> proxy port"]

        User --> CLI
        CLI -- "starts on a background thread<br/>inside the CLI's own process" --> ProxyThread
        CLI -- "spawns as a CHILD PROCESS,<br/>pointed at loopback proxy port" --> CC2
        CC2 -- "Anthropic-shaped HTTP<br/>to 127.0.0.1:port" --> ProxyThread
    end

    Ollama[["Ollama<br/>http://127.0.0.1:11434<br/>ONE instance, shared by both trees<br/>and by the one-shot CLI below"]]

    OneShot["localgpu prompt<br/>(one-shot, no tree)<br/>ungrounded, spawns nothing"]

    Server -- "HTTP loopback<br/>ollama.py: embed()" --> Ollama
    ProxyThread -- "HTTP loopback<br/>anthropic_proxy.py: chat, keep_alive=5m<br/>DEFAULT_KEEP_ALIVE (plugin/localgpu/cli/anthropic_proxy.py:50)" --> Ollama
    OneShot -- "HTTP loopback<br/>ollama.py: generate(), keep_alive=30s<br/>(plugin/localgpu/mcp/ollama.py:26) - deliberately<br/>NOT the shell's 5m lease" --> Ollama

    Constraint["OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS=1<br/>ONE Ollama keeps one<br/>8GB-VRAM model resident"]
    Ollama -.-> Constraint

    style Ollama fill:#4a5568,stroke:#2d3748,color:#fff

Data flow crew config autoclear

context.autoClear: how its settings are read straight from both raw files (not through resolve_config), and how its writer refuses a malformed machine file before handing off to the shared writer.

        direction TB
        ACREAD["<b>crew_autocycle.settings(root)</b><br/>reads BOTH raw files directly,<br/>NOT resolve_config"]
        ACWRITE["<b>crew_autoclear_setup.py</b><br/>write_autoclear_method() /<br/>write_autoclear_enabled()"]
        ACCHECK{"global file<br/>readable?"}
        ACRAISE>"<b>GlobalConfigUnreadable</b><br/>refuses to write over<br/>a malformed global file"]
        ACGO["<b>crew_config.</b><br/><b>write_global_config()</b><br/>the SAME atomic writer"]
    end
    ACWRITE --> ACCHECK
    ACCHECK -->|malformed| ACRAISE
    ACCHECK -->|ok or absent| ACGO

Data flow crew config menu

The /crew:config menu (its rows, choices, Save, and repo-file delete and restore) and the one file layer every crew config write goes through: lock, compare-and-swap update, no-clobber move.

flowchart TB

    subgraph Files["NEW (T-0075): the one file layer - plugin/crew/hooks/scripts/crew_config_files.py"]
        direction TB
        FLOCK["<b>Lock</b> :104<br/>&lt;path&gt;.lock holding the PID;<br/>machine_lock() first"]
        FUPD["<b>update_json()</b> :364<br/>read, compare digest, mutate,<br/>replace - inside the lock"]
        FMOVE["<b>move_no_clobber()</b> :466<br/>a rename that NEVER<br/>replaces its destination"]
        FREST["<b>read_restorable()</b> :199<br/>the ONE read delete refuses by<br/>and restore accepts by"]
        FLOCK --- FUPD
    end
    subgraph Menu["NEW (T-0075): the /crew:config menu - plugin/crew/hooks/scripts/crew_config_menu.py"]
        direction TB
        MSPEC["<b>menu_spec()</b> :317<br/>rows from the layer's template"]
        MCHOICE["<b>choices()</b> :215<br/>a value is offered only when<br/>the layer's planner accepts it"]
        MSAVE["<b>save()</b> :480<br/>plans BOTH layers<br/>before writing either"]
        MPLAN["<b>plan_delete()</b> :800<br/>holds the file's bytes and digests;<br/>delete_preview()"]
        MDEL["<b>apply_delete()</b> :852<br/>move_aside() to<br/>.crew/config.json.bak-UTC"]
        MREST["<b>restore_repo_config()</b> :962<br/>moves any current file aside,<br/>create_bytes()"]
        MSPEC --> MCHOICE
        MCHOICE --> MSAVE
        MPLAN --> MDEL
    end
    MDEL --> FMOVE
    MREST --> FMOVE
    FREST -.-> MPLAN
    FREST -.-> MREST
BoxDetails
FLOCKLock :104 - O_CREAT|O_EXCL <path>.lock holding the PID (a failed PID write removes it, :134-141); Busy :63 after LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS :43. Serialises crew's writers, not a hand edit. machine_lock() :273 is the machine file's Lock, ALWAYS taken (creates ~/.claude/crew/, never the file), before any repo Lock - one nesting order
FUPDupdate_json() :364 - inside the lock: read_strict() :181 (absent / unparsable / empty / notobject), state_digest() :243 (ABSENT :50 for no file) compared with expect (Conflict :67), mutate, replace_text() :352 (sibling, fsync, os.replace, CRLF and BOM kept)
FMOVEmove_no_clobber() :466 - a rename that NEVER replaces its destination: os.link, then _unlink_source() :418 renames the source to a reserved name and removes it only when it IS the linked inode; a foreign file is linked back and its *.moving name KEPT (Displaced :71, exit 1; the link to the backup is never undone after the rename). move_aside() :508 (the backup IS the inode), create_bytes() :517
FRESTread_restorable() :199 - a REGULAR file that restorable() :171 accepts: the ONE read delete refuses by and restore accepts by
MSPECmenu_spec() :317 rows = leaf_paths(default_global_config()) (machine, plus platform.* and schema read-only) / leaf_paths(default_config()) (repo); returns the layer file's digest
MCHOICEchoices() :215 - a value is offered only when _probe_for() :168 accepts it: the layer's own planner on one snapshot, with the --pending set plus the candidate; all refused = a read-only row naming the key to fix
MSAVEsave() :480 _plan_both() :446 plans BOTH layers before writing either (the repo against the machine as this Save leaves it), prints the machine digest whenever anything changes, checks every given --expect-* before either write and binds each writer, the repo write to the machine digest too
MPLANplan_delete() :800 - holds the file's bytes, its digest, the machine digest and machinePath; refuses what read_restorable() refuses (a symlink included); delete_preview() :637 walks the file's OWN leaves too (removed / re-detected - only the platform keys platform-sync writes, _redetected() :629 - / held by the ratchet)
MDELapply_delete() :852 - typed repo name AND both preview digests (_unbound() :836), then under machine_lock and then the repo Lock the machine digest AGAIN (changed: exit 2, nothing deleted), move_aside() to .crew/config.json.bak-UTC, compare with the held bytes (changed: moved back no-clobber, nothing deleted); prints three restore lines, sh / cmd / PowerShell (restore_lines :773)
MRESTrestore_repo_config() :962 - _valid_backup() :946 then read_restorable(); under the Lock moves any current file aside (Displaced: exit 1, every path named), create_bytes() (never over a file that appeared), reads back

Data flow crew config no python

What two guards do when they cannot find python: role-write-guard.sh cannot read guards.roleWrites, so it always blocks a restricted role; cloud-guard.sh reads cloudGuard crudely from the resolved repo file and the machine file, and refuses when armed or when git cannot name a lane's main checkout.

flowchart LR

    subgraph NoPython["role-write-guard.sh's no-python fallback - a NARROWER contract than the old one"]
        direction TB
        NP1["<b>_resolve_role_write_python()</b><br/>finds no usable interpreter"]
        NP2["<b>_role_write_fallback_decision()</b><br/>cannot evaluate<br/>guards.roleWrites at all"]
        NP3["Unrestricted role: allowed.<br/>Restricted or unreadable role:<br/>ALWAYS BLOCKED (exit 2)"]
        NP1 --> NP2 --> NP3
    end

    subgraph CloudNoPython["cloud-guard's fallback - reads the resolved repo file (T-0096)"]
        direction TB
        CG1["no usable python,<br/>or cloud_guard.py failed"]
        CG2["<b>_cloud_guard_armed</b><br/>resolved repo file +<br/>machine file"]
        CG3["unknown, or cloudGuard<br/>not off: REFUSED (exit 2)"]
        CG1 --> CG2 --> CG3
    end
BoxDetails
NP1_resolve_role_write_python() plugin/crew/hooks/scripts/role-write-guard.sh:44- fails to find a usable interpreter
NP2_role_write_fallback_decision() :326-346. Cannot evaluate guards.roleWrites (off/report/pm's own path allowances) at all - only tells a restricted role from an unrestricted one via the deny-list mirror
NP3Unrestricted role: allowed unjudged. Restricted role (pm or _DENY_ROLES) OR a role this fallback could not even read: ALWAYS BLOCKED (exit 2), regardless of what guards.roleWrites actually says :339-345
CG1crew_py_strict plugin/crew/hooks/scripts/_common.sh finds no usable interpreter, or cloud_guard.py exits non-zero (cloud-guard.sh:55-78)
CG2_cloud_guard_armed plugin/crew/hooks/scripts/cloud-guard.sh:40; armed when the resolver is missing. The repo file is crew_repo_config_dir's (_common.sh:328): a lane with no config of its own reads the main checkout's. Twin: Test-CloudGuardArmed in cloud-guard.ps1 through Get-CrewRepoConfigDir.
CG3source unknown, or any cloudGuard value other than off in either file: exit 2 (refuse). Otherwise exit 0, unjudged.

Data flow crew config ratchet

The keys that do not follow repo-beats-global: the two ratchet tables (read side and write side), the thirteen keys that resolve by the lower rank, and how a corrupt config file forces the role-write guard to block.

flowchart TB

    subgraph Ratchet["Two DIFFERENT ratchet tables, not one - 14 write-side, 13 read-side"]
        direction TB
        RG["<b>READ side:</b><br/>crew_guards.RATCHETED_KEYS<br/>13 keys"]
        RC["<b>WRITE side:</b><br/>crew_config._RATCHETED<br/>14 keys: the thirteen + pm.authority"]
        RSHAPE["Confirmed by import + diff + type():<br/>tuple field order differs, so<br/>not one table as written"]
        RG --- RC --- RSHAPE
    end
    subgraph Corrupt["A corrupt config file is its own state, and it BEATS the ratchet"]
        direction TB
        LS["<b>crew_config.layer_state(path)</b><br/>absent / corrupt / ok,<br/>either layer"]
        FORCE["<b>role_write_guard.py</b><br/>corruption in either layer<br/>forces policy = block"]
        LS --> FORCE
    end
    FORCE -.->|"overrides the resolved value"| Ratchet
    subgraph Except["Thirteen keys do NOT follow the precedence above (read-side ratchet)"]
        direction TB
        E1["<b>13 RATCHETED_KEYS</b><br/>resolve by the LOWER rank,<br/>not by repo-beats-global"]
        E2["effective value = the<br/><b>lower-ranked</b> of the two layers<br/>effective_ratcheted :564"]
        E3["Why: crew reads config<br/>out of CLONED repositories"]
        E4["Absent = the narrowest tier<br/>for ELEVEN of the thirteen"]
        E5["<b>guards.roleWrites, guards.cloudGuard</b><br/>the two exceptions to E4:<br/>DEFAULT is not their FLOOR"]
        E6["install.policy: auto is safe -<br/>no repo string becomes a command<br/>(crew_guards.INSTALLABLE)"]
        E1 --- E2 --- E3 --- E4 --- E5 --- E6
    end
BoxDetails
RGREAD side: crew_guards.RATCHETED_KEYS plugin/crew/hooks/scripts/crew_guards.py:522-549 13 keys (executed + len()'d, this pass): install.policy, change.requireForProduction, environments.prodUnattended (T-0005), and all TEN guards.* - terraformApply, forcePush, adminMerge, mergeGate, cloudDestructive, sqlDestructive, prodDatabase, prodServer, roleWrites, cloudGuard (new). Consumed by crew_config.resolve_ratcheted() :831 via crew_guards.effective_ratcheted() :564, called at crew_config.py:875
RCWRITE side: crew_config._RATCHETED plugin/crew/hooks/scripts/crew_config.py:2527 (extended through :2622) 14 keys: the same thirteen PLUS pm.authority. pm.authority is still NOT in RATCHETED_KEYS - it resolves by ordinary precedence and only needs a widening NOTE when /crew:config writes it
RSHAPEConfirmed by import + diff + type(), not asserted: 13-key intersection, pm.authority the only difference (`set(_RATCHETED) - set(RATCHETED_KEYS) == {'pm.authority'}`), and the tuple field order STILL differs -- (function, function, dict) here, (tuple, function, function) there -- so the two still cannot be collapsed into one table as written
LScrew_config.layer_state(path) plugin/crew/hooks/scripts/crew_config.py:937 classifies ONE config file, either layer (cloud=True / environments=True - the cloud guard's reads only - also call a malformed cloud / environments block corrupt): absent - nothing there (os.path.lexists false, so a DANGLING SYMLINK is corrupt, not absent). corrupt - present but not the shape this key needs: unreadable, invalid JSON, not an object, or an object where "guards" in parsed and guards is not itself a dict (an EXPLICIT null is corrupt, not an unset key). ok - everything else
FORCEplugin/crew/hooks/scripts/role_write_guard.py calls layer_state for BOTH layers at :760-761, ORs them into forced_by_corruption :762, and sets policy = "block" UNCONDITIONALLY at :764-765 -- BEFORE the elif policy == "off": return 0 early exit at :766-767
E1Every key in crew_guards.RATCHETED_KEYS :522-549 -- install.policy, change.requireForProduction, environments.prodUnattended and all TEN guards.* -- resolves by the LOWER rank, not by repo-beats-global. CONFIG.md section 15 covers install.policy, section 16 the guards, section 18 guards.roleWrites; environments.* is a subsection of section 16.
E2The effective value at each key is the lower-ranked of the two layers - crew_guards.effective_ratcheted :564, reached through crew_config.resolve_ratcheted :831.
E3Why: crew reads config out of CLONED repositories. A repo shipping install.policy: auto, or guards.cloudGuard: report, would, under precedence, override a machine owner who chose manual or off.
E4Absent counts as the narrowest tier on either side for ELEVEN of the thirteen, so the WIDEST grant requires BOTH layers to agree.
E5guards.roleWrites and guards.cloudGuard are the two exceptions to E4, and the only keys here whose DEFAULT is not their FLOOR. ROLE_WRITE_POLICIES is (block, report, off); ROLE_WRITE_DEFAULT is off, the WIDEST tier, for both names - cloudGuard reuses roleWrites' own normalise/rank functions rather than growing a second copy (crew_guards.py:450-487, guard_tiers() :490-504).
E6install.policy: auto is safe only because no repo-controlled string can become a command - crew_guards.INSTALLABLE maps a name to a literal argv tuple, consulted BEFORE the policy. Asserted in tests/test_install_policy.py.

Data flow crew config shell route

How the two kinds of source, a Mermaid fence in Markdown and a standalone .mmd file, are collected into one sorted list, including how a fence is extracted to a sidecar .mmd without changing any other line ending.

flowchart TB

        direction TB
        MD["a Markdown file with a<br/>```mermaid fence<br/>FENCE_RE :44-49 - indent-aware, and the<br/>closing fence must match the opener"]
        MMD["a standalone .mmd / .mermaid file<br/>walk() :129-136"]
    end

    EXTRACT["process_markdown() :369-437<br/>writes a sidecar .mmd per block<br/><b>Idempotent by construction</b>"]
    EXTRACT2["<b>NEW in 1.2.5:<br/>_normalize_with_offsets() :335-366</b><br/>untouched lines keep their terminator"]
    NAME["stem = slug(md stem)-NN[-slug(heading)]<br/>heading_before() :328-332"]

    EXTRACT --- EXTRACT2
    EXTRACT --> NAME
    NAME --> POOL
    MMD --> POOL

BoxDetails
MMDskips DEFAULT_EXCLUDES :42 (.git, node_modules, .venv, venv, vendor, dist, build, .tox)
EXTRACT(newline="\n" pinned :410) and rewrites the fence into an image link. Idempotent by construction: once the fence is gone there is nothing left for FENCE_RE to match, so re-runs are no-ops - the file is not marked, the evidence is the absence itself
EXTRACT2Every line the rewrite does NOT touch keeps its own original terminator - CRLF, LF, bare CR, or no trailing newline at all. Before: the whole file was read with read_text() (which collapses every terminator to "\n") and written back the same way - so one CRLF line in a mostly-LF file flipped every OTHER line to CRLF too. Now: raw_text is decoded but NOT collapsed; a parallel normalized copy is built for FENCE_RE/HEADING_RE matching, and an offset map lets pass-through spans be sliced out of raw_text :412, :427 instead. The one line the function DOES write - the inserted image link - takes the terminator that already ended the fence's own closing line :413-422, then the whole result is written with newline="" :435 so nothing gets re-translated at write time. Regressions: tests/test_check_reads_the_svg.py :460 (preserves CRLF convention), :602 (preserves CRLF after the last fence), :582 (adds no trailing newline), :638 (sidecar content correct for a CRLF source)
NAMEwalks every heading before the block and keeps the LAST, so the filename says which section it came from

P1A) verify-diagrams, RECOMMENDED. python:3.11-slim, one line: python scripts/render_mermaid.py . --check No push credentials, no commit loop, and the diff lands in review where a human can see it. Never reaches resolve_mmdc at all - which is why the WinError 2 above was a developer-machine and strategy-B failure, invisible to strategy A
P2in its own header: a repo whose manifest predates version 2 fails the first run, and --force is REQUIRED to fix it because the source hash already matches and a plain run would skip them. The script's own message says the same thing. Two places, one sentence - deliberately, because whichever one a reader hits first has to be enough.
P3Needs write access and [skip ci], or the commit retriggers the pipeline. fonts-liberation is not optional: Chromium in a slim image has no fonts, mermaid MEASURES text to lay out nodes, and no fonts means every label is mis-sized and the boxes overlap.
ORDERBitbucket Cloud has never rendered Mermaid in Markdown (BCLOUD-21675, open for years); a fenced block shows as raw source. The .mmd stays the reviewable artifact and the .svg is a build product that happens to be committed - which is why the manifest exists to say whether the two still agree.

R0subprocess.run wrapped in try/except OSError :262-273. resolve_mmdc already returned a path that EXISTS; this is the separate question of whether it RUNS - a shim pointing at a deleted install, a wrong-architecture binary, a lost execute bit
R1built at :251-258 --backgroundColor :256 (default #ffffff, opaque so diagrams stay legible against dark mode) --quiet :257, --puppeteerConfigFile :259-260 when one exists
R5strip mermaid's max-width style :307, then write the file back with newline="\n" :321 pinned (NEW in 1.2.5) - the write no longer turns LF into CRLF on Windows. It does NOT make raw SVG bytes reproducible across platforms (render_mermaid.py:93-94, and the TODO.md bullet "Real mmdc output has nothing for a line-ending translation to act on"). Regression: tests/test_check_reads_the_svg.py:345
TOOLGONEAn unusable launcher is unusable for EVERY diagram, so falling through to the per-file failed list would retry each one and bury the message under N copies of the same error. The resolved path is printed alongside it :273, because 'mmdc not found' is confusing on a machine where it demonstrably was.
FAILand both exit 1 :602 - mmdc exiting non-zero :274-276, and an SVG that would be blank-labelled in Bitbucket :295-300. The config sets htmlLabels:false, but a source can re-enable it with an inline %%{init}%% directive, so the output is checked rather than the config trusted.
WRITEnever before - which is also why svg_digest reads the file at that moment and not the one render() produced

FCthen the script's own neighbours. Exits with the list it tried, and says WHY defaults are not acceptable :206-207: mmdc's defaults emit foreignObject labels
RM- :239-241 for the mmdc branch, :242-244 for npx - not the bare name. It used to test if shutil.which("mmdc") for truthiness and then hand subprocess the literal string "mmdc". which consults PATHEXT; CreateProcess does not - it searches for the literal name and name+.exe only - so Windows' mmdc.cmd was FOUND and then could not be SPAWNED: WinError 2 on a machine where mermaid-cli was installed. Both branches had the bug; the npx fallback is fixed too. Falling through exits with MMDC_MISSING :220-224 at :245 - MMDC_MISSING is now a shared module-level constant, reused by render()'s OSError handler too

BoxDetails
H3trailing space and leading and trailing blank lines stripped - a whitespace edit must not cost a re-render
H4digest() covers the source only. The artifact is covered separately by svgHash - svg_digest() :77-97, recorded at render time :548-549 and compared on --check :528. NEW in 1.2.5: svg_digest() also folds CRLF/CR to LF before hashing :96-97, not just at write time - closes a false DAMAGED on a Windows clone with core.autocrlf=true (no .gitattributes entry marks *.svg as binary here), which checks out the committed LF bytes as CRLF and would otherwise hash differently from what was recorded. Regression: tests/test_check_reads_the_svg.py:276 (test_check_tolerates_a_crlf_checkout_of_a_committed_svg). Its own subtlety, unchanged: the hash is taken AFTER postprocess(), which REWRITES the SVG. Hashing before would record a digest the file never has.
MANIFESTAn unreadable manifest is a warning, not an error - it degrades to 'nothing is current', which re-renders rather than silently skipping. save() :166-173 now pins newline="\n" :172-173 - a Windows-rendered manifest is byte-identical to a Linux one for the same JSON. Regression: tests/test_check_reads_the_svg.py:381

Process crew lifecycle review

/crew:review: the preflight, pre-review and self-check gates that run before a round is spent, then the review rounds and their verdicts, ending in a receipt or NEEDS_REPLAN.

flowchart TB
    subgraph review["/crew:review - two rounds per ticket"]
        pf0{"preflight (#264):<br/>receipt, gate, budget?"}
        pf0 -- "CLEAN receipt: CLEAN,<br/>no round, no self-check" --> rcpt
        pf0 -- "gate not passed or unknown:<br/>exit 5, no round spent,<br/>self-check not asked<br/>review.md:449" --> vg0["run the verify gate,<br/>then review again"]
        vg0 --> to_im5
        pf0 -- "go on" --> pr0{"pre-review checks<br/>pass? (L-0574)"}
        pr0 -- "NEW finding or COULD NOT CHECK:<br/>exit 5, no round spent<br/>review.md:449" --> fx0["fix the finding or the tool,<br/>then review again"]
        fx0 --> to_im5
        pr0 -- "pass / n/a / none configured,<br/>override recorded, or an active<br/>incident (skip logged)" --> rv0{"self-check<br/>stamped?"}
        pf0 -- "no rounds left or NEEDS_REPLAN:<br/>budget refusal answers first<br/>review_run.py:850-861" --> replan
        rv0 -- "no: exit 2,<br/>no round spent<br/>review.md:446-449" --> to_sc1
        rv0 -- "yes (or no approval receipt,<br/>or an incident: skip logged)" --> rv1["reserve a round, run<br/>Codex / Copilot /<br/>crew:reviewer fallback<br/>review.md:25-28, :451"]
        rv1 --> rv2{"verdict (the script's)<br/>:440, :482-486"}
        rv2 -- "CLEAN (exact: no other line)" --> rcpt["receipt written<br/>:510"]
        rv2 -- "FINDINGS (stray prose<br/>ignored and named)" --> rv3{"final round,<br/>0 BLOCK?"}
        rv3 -- "auto-accept or owner :508" --> rcpt
        rv3 -- "fix, round 2" --> again_rv1
        rv2 -- "INCOMPLETE (tool failure: refunded, :485-486)" --> again_rv1
        rv2 -- "INCOMPLETE (reviewer / tree, a contract-like<br/>or shortfall stray line): counts" --> again_rv1
        rv2 -- "third round refused" --> replan([NEEDS_REPLAN:<br/>back to /crew:plan<br/>or autopilot auto-reject])
    end

    again_rv1>"again: reserve a round,<br/>run the reviewers (above)"]
    to_im5>"back: implement part<br/>then /crew:review last"]
    to_sc1>"back: implement part<br/>required standards self-check"]
    rcpt --> to_dn1>"next: done part<br/>1 review receipt"]

pf0preflight first (#264): a CLEAN receipt covers this bundle? verify gate passed this tree? review_run.py:672, :846
pr0no linter finding the bundle adds against its base? could every configured linter check? review_run.py prereview_gate :731

pf0->replanthe budget refusal answers first, no pre-review checks, no self-check

replanalso reached from rv3 under autopilot (T-0074): out of rounds with a BLOCK, autopilot.maxAutoReplans 1 or more and the successor plan self-approvable, crew_autopilot.py auto-reject (auto_replan_policy) rejects it; at the cap it stops for the owner

Process crew lifecycle spec plan

/crew:spec writes spec.md from the approved direction, then /crew:plan writes plan.md, amending the spec's Touch list first when a step reaches outside it, and stops for approval.

flowchart TB
    subgraph spec["/crew:spec"]
        sp1{"direction.md?<br/>spec.md:10"}
        sp1 -- missing --> spx([refuse: run /crew:brainstorm])
        sp1 -- yes --> sp2["write spec.md<br/>Touch one path per bullet<br/>:15, :38-43"]
        sp2 --> sp3["crew_tracker.py move --to spec<br/>:45-48"]
    end

    subgraph plan["/crew:plan"]
        sp3 --> pl1["write plan.md: steps with<br/>Files / Test / Risk / Standards<br/>plan.md:27, :36"]
        pl1 --> pl2{"every Files: entry<br/>inside Touch?<br/>:44"}
        pl2 -- no --> amend["amend spec Touch first<br/>spec.md:57"]
        amend --> pl1
        pl2 -- yes --> pl3["show the plan, STOP<br/>:49"]
    end

    pl3 --> to_ap0>"next: approve part<br/>user types /crew:approve id"]

localgpu: /localgpu:setup (7 steps, agent-driven) calls bootstrap.{sh,ps1} (6 steps, script-driven). NOTE: ground truth handed to this lane said "six-step" setup flow; commands/setup.md actually says "Seven steps, in order" (plugin/localgpu/commands/setup.md:7) - corrected here, see report.

S1prints resolved path, flags WSL cross-filesystem case

S7reports what changed, points at /localgpu:index, runs /localgpu:doctor
